verdicts.flaw_description: The named alternative cause reaches the units: "Rainfall in each block's season ran to roughly double the year before, and every block lay in open ground, taking rain as it fell." Doubled rainfall falling directly on open-ground maize blocks could produce the 0.4-0.7 t/ha gains regardless of the drip line.

The measurement windows run backwards from installation: plot one was "boxed 3 June" but counted "by 27 March" against the previous spring, and plot three was "boxed 2 November" but counted "by 24 September" against the previous autumn, so the fledging counts close before the boxes were installed.

A competing cause reaches the classes: "Class sizes at each school fell by half from the year before, and every logged class took its English lessons as one whole group" — so English was taught to groups half their former size, and the 5-9 point comprehension gains could come from the halved class size rather than the reading program.

The reported figures cover a narrower population than the claim: "Pass rates cover the students entered for the exam, and about a quarter of each cohort's roll was not entered." With a quarter of each roll excluded from the denominator, the 4-8 point rises could reflect which students were entered rather than any improvement from the tutoring blocks.
